Q: Thank you for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement concerns the rear-end collision in
Pasadena, Texas. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd prefer to just go by my first name for now, if that's all right.
Q: That's fine. Can you describe where you were sitting when the collision happened?
A: I was in the front passenger seat of a sedan. My friend was driving us home from an errand.
Q: Were you wearing a seatbelt?
A: Yes, I had it on the whole time.
Q: Tell me what happened right before impact.
A: We were stopped at a red light on a main road. I looked in the side mirror and saw a pickup coming up fast. I
remember thinking it wasn't going to stop in time. Then it hit us from behind.
Q: Did your body move in any particular way?
A: Yes, my knee slammed into the dashboard. My head went forward and then snapped back against the seat.
Q: Did you get out of the vehicle or receive any treatment at the scene?
A: Paramedics came. I told them my knee was hurting badly, and they checked me over. I didn't go by ambulance,
though. My friend drove me to a clinic later.
Q: Have you seen a doctor since then?
A: Yes, I've been to the clinic twice now. They took X-rays and said there's swelling and some ligament strain. I've
been icing it and using a brace.
Q: Has the knee affected your daily activities?
A: Definitely. Stairs are hard, and I can't work my shift at the warehouse right now. It makes it difficult to sleep too.
Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add?
A: Only that I want to make sure my medical bills get covered. I'm willing to send you my records.
Q: Thank you. We'll follow up with a request for those records. This concludes the statement.
</page>

it is the loss date. Examples: "Date of loss:", "Crash date:", "Date of injury:", "the collision on".
